_meta.purpose: Maps Codeforces problem tags -> MarkTrace concept-graph node ids. Finalized against dsa_concept_graph.json v2.0 (43 nodes).
_meta.design_rule: Map each CF tag to the MOST SPECIFIC concept it represents. Do NOT inject upstream concepts (e.g. recursion). The engine's graph traversal (stage3 = weak concepts + their conceptual ancestors) already surfaces the upstream root. That is the whole point of the concept graph - let it do the tracing.
_meta.no_recursion_tag_note: Codeforces has NO 'recursion' tag. Recursion weakness is inferred by the engine: weak dp / divide_conquer / dfs all have 'recursion' as a CONCEPTUAL ancestor in your graph, so the engine promotes recursion to a candidate root on its own. Trust the graph, don't force it here.
_meta.verified: Every concept id below was checked to exist as a node in dsa_concept_graph.json v2.0.
_meta.deleted_because_no_node: number theory, math, combinatorics, bitmasks (no bit_manipulation node), data structures (too broad -> noise), linked list (not a real CF tag). These CF tags now correctly contribute NO signal.
_meta.watch: 'sortings' -> basic_sorting is the loosest mapping (CF sorting problems are about USING order, not bubble/selection). Revisit if diagnoses over-blame basic_sorting.
